cited_evidence: Top-level corpus has source_weight values distinct from demand_score, e.g. n06-r01 demand_score 9 with source_weight 5 and n06-r08 demand_score 3 with source_weight 2.
Job 2 input needs/evidence_sources show n06-r01 source_weight 9 and n06-r08 source_weight 3, matching demand_score rather than the stipulated source_weight.
Upstream function select_demand source appends "source_weight": row.get('demand_score', 0), directly explaining the corrupted handoff.
initial_receipt.explanation: The execution fails to preserve source_weight from the stipulated corpus. The downstream job received source_weight values equal to demand_score, so the fault was introduced upstream before the exact handoff. The supplied upstream source localizes this to select_demand, which writes source_weight from row.get('demand_score', 0) instead of row.get('source_weight', 0).
